item.title: Is AI Actually Going to Kill Us All?
item.description: This week on “Uncanny Valley,” we dig into a former Anthropic researcher’s AI doomsday warning, the latest upgrades from Apple’s event, and the census report that claimed Trump won the 2020 election.

item.title: Don't buy the 'regular' AirPods 5

item.title: Schools are catching on to Big Tech’s playbook
item.description: It's the hot new thing in tech, and it's where all the jobs are. Students who don't learn to use it fall behind. And to help them catch up in time, its creators are graciously providing the resources and curriculum for learning it, often pro bono. That's the narrative AI companies are pitching schools on […]

item.description: Development of a dedicated AI agent specifically designed for automated research tasks has been confirmed by OpenAI.

item.title: Companies deploying AI agents have ‘no idea how to manage risk,’ AI safety expert warns
item.description: The warning comes a day after one Anthropic researcher resigned over concerns that rapidly improving AI could threaten the human species. Business leaders are accelerating the deployment of agentic artificial intelligence with “no idea how to manage risk,” an AI safety expert warned yesterday.

item.title: Travel scams are getting smarter. Here’s how to protect yourself

item.title: FBI launches investigation after 153 million drivers licenses apparently leaked on Russian cybercrime forum
item.description: Lousiana-based identity verification service IDScan identified as the target of a hack that leaked 153 million US drivers licenses.

item.title: USPS is launching new $20 stamp books in October. Here’s why they cost more
item.description: The Postal Service’s newest stamps arrive Oct. 6, but a book will cost more than standard Forever stamps for an important reason. The United States Postal Service (USPS) will soon issue a new semipostal stamp — a fundraising stamp that covers the cost of postage plus an amount dedicated to charity — aimed at raising money for fentanyl awareness.

item.title: IDScan is offering free credit monitoring and ID protection after leaking driver's licenses
item.description: The platform was linked to an FBI investigation into a dark web marketplace last week.
